top_signals.title: Brent Holds Above $102 as Gulf Export Rebound Offsets U.S. Military Moves
top_signals.summary: Crude oil prices are set for a modest weekly decline today, as reports of a strong rebound in oil flows out of the Persian Gulf trumped news of more U.S. troops moving to the Middle East and China’s Thursday decision to halt fuel exports this month. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $102.24 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate was trading at $92.62. Both benchmarks posted strong gains in September and while the start to October has been lower, if hostilities in the Persian Gulf escalate again, the upward potential will…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: New Indonesia Finance Chief Steers Clear of Prabowo Turf Wars
top_signals.summary: Indonesia’s new finance chief signaled he’ll stay in his lane and let the central bank and the Danantara sovereign wealth fund handle their own mandates, a bid to restore investor confidence in President Prabowo Subianto’s broad economic policy.
